text: Write the opening of a story called On The Run, about a person who has to change their identity
and move to a new location. In your writing, create a sense of mystery and apprehension.
Write two contrasting pieces (300–450 words each): the first about an astronaut in space, looking
down on Earth; and the second about a young child on Earth, looking up at the moon. In your
writing, focus on the feelings of each person, and create a sense of wonder.
Write a descriptive piece called The Skyscraper. In your writing, focus on the light, and the colour
and scale of the building to help your reader imagine the scene.
Section B: Writing for an audience
You recently went to a music festival in your country. Write a review of the festival, which will be
published in your school magazine.
Two speakers are going to take part in a debate on homework. One of the speakers recognises
the benefits of homework; the other speaker feels that students should not have to do more
schoolwork at home. Write the texts of their speeches (300–450 words each).
Write the voiceover script for a TV report on a popular local event. The script should cover part
of the event itself, and some brief discussion of it afterwards. In your writing, create a sense of
atmosphere and enjoyment.
